question.text: The Magna Carta was signed by this king, the youngest of five sons of Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine.
question.clue: He failed to reclaim Normandy from France after his allies lost to Philip Augustus at the battle of Bouvines.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about famous British explorers who died or disappeared while on their voyages.
swap.text: This navigator searched for a Northwest Passage to Asia while sailing the ship Half-Moon on behalf of the Dutch East India Company. This explorer mysteriously disappeared after a 1611 mutiny aboard his ship.
swap.clue: This captain of the Hopewell laid the foundation for the creation of New Netherland through a 1609 exploration.

question.text: This radical secret society of textile workers destroyed looms and other machines that were replacing them in England in the 1810s. Its name is used today for anyone resistant to technological change.
question.clue: Like the Swing Riots, this movement was inspired by a mythological king or general.

swap.leadin: This war ended with the creation of the Protectorate and the execution of King Charles I.
swap.text: Name this war, which saw a clash between factions known as the Cavaliers and Roundheads. The Long Parliament essentially ruled its namesake country during this war.
swap.clue: One figure formed a cavalry unit called "Ironsides."

question.text: Lord Raglan's misinterpreted order in this 1852 battle led to General Cardigan's disastrous Charge of the Light Brigade.
question.clue: During it, Sir Colin Campbell's 93rd Highland Regiment repelled an enemy attack in the "Thin Red Line" defense.

swap.text: From his exile in Portugal, Pedro called for the end of this system, which was weakened by the Law of Sexagenarians and the Law of the Free Womb before finally being abolished by the Golden Law in 1888.
swap.clue: William Wilberforce famously campaigned against this practice whose horrors were described by Olaudah Equiano.

question.leadin: FTPE, name some modern British capital-C Conservatives.
question.text: This Epping M.P. succeeded Neville Chamberlain and, offering nothing but "blood, toil, tears, and sweat," led the British to victory in the Second World War.
question.clue: Clement Attlee replaced this man at the Potsdam Conference after the Conservatives were voted out in July 1945.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the royalty of England.
swap.text: This English king was the first of the house of Tudor, ending the Plantagenet dynasty by overthrowing Richard III. His reign ushered in economic growth in England, and he was succeeded by his son who led the English reformation.
swap.clue: This ruler ordered the repeal of the Titulus Regius of his predecessor, who had seized the throne by imprisoning two princes in the Tower of London.

question.leadin: During this event, Flemish people were supposedly massacred for not pronouncing "bread and cheese" correctly.
question.text: Name this 1381 uprising of poor farmers against Richard II, which was led by Wat Tyler in response to an increased poll tax.
question.clue: Simon Sudbury, the Archbishop of Canterbury, was executed during this event.

swap.leadin: T-Bonus 1. His minor works include a paper on calculating the correct period for celebrating holidays, "On the Reckoning of Time."
swap.text: Name this monk of Jarrow who summarized five centuries, from Caesar's arrival to Christianization by Augustine of Canterbury, in his Ecclesiastical History of the English People.
swap.clue: Working for thirty years at St. Paul's Monastery at Jarrow, his hagiographies include On the Lives of Abbots and a credulous account of the miracles of St. Cuthbert.

question.text: Before gaining a peerage in the House of Lords, Wellington was elected to the House of Commons from one of these districts nicknamed for being so small that a person could bribe nearly all voters. They were eliminated by the Reform Act of 1832.
question.clue: Eventually, all fifty-six were eliminated, affecting an average of only thirty-nine people per district.

swap.leadin: He was introduced to Christine Keeler at a party, unaware that she was already involved with Soviet military emissary Eugene Ivanov.
swap.text: Name this British Secretary of State for War whose affair with Keeler sparked an espionage scandal in 1963.
swap.clue: In 1960, this man was appointed to the position of Secretary of State for War by Harold Macmillan.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the different things people did in medieval Europe to amuse themselves and kill time.
question.text: The Old English Bulldog was raised for this blood sport that involved violence between dogs and bulls. Tudor rulers Henry VIII and Elizabeth I enjoyed a popular version of this practice that used bears.

swap.text: For his handling of the financial crisis, Paul Krugman credited this Labour Prime Minister with having "saved the world financial system." This former Chancellor of the Exchequer succeeded Tony Blair.
swap.clue: John Prescott said this man has the "worst smile in the world," a reference to his frequent grinning during Youtube videos in which he explains policy decisions.

question.leadin: The lexicographer Daniel Silvan Evans began publishing an extensive dictionary of this language in 1887.
question.text: Name this language, which Saunder Lewis promoted in a 1962 radio speech titled The Fate of the Language.
question.clue: Advocates for this language including Saunders Lewis were imprisoned for protesting an air force base constructed under Stanley Baldwin.

swap.leadin: This person's army defeated that of Ralph the Timid, and then sacked the city of Hereford.
swap.text: Name this person, who conquered Deheubarth in 1055 to become the only native Welsh ruler to unite all of Wales, and as such is regarded as the only King of Wales.
swap.answerHtml: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn [‘Griffith’ ap ‘Clew-well-in’; prompt on partial answer]

question.text: This son of Emma of Normandy and half-brother of Harold Harefoot ordered the Harrying of Worcestshire after two of his hosuecarls were murdered. This king's name translates as "Tough-knot" and he was succeeded by Edward the Confessor as King of England.

swap.leadin: The proto-Welsh king Cadafael earned the disrespectful sobriquet "battle-shirker" for abandoning this king at the Battle of Winwaed.
swap.text: Name this seventh-century king who defeated Oswald of Northumbria at the excellently-named Battle of Maserfield, establishing the supremacy of Mercia in the Heptarchy.
swap.clue: This man, one of the last pagan kings of England, whose son Wulfhere would later assume the throne of his kingdom after rebelling against the Northumbrian Oswy.

question.text: Whitehouse coined this term for lurid exploitation videos during her "Clean Up TV" campaign. These videos were blamed for the Hungerford massacre during a 1980s moral panic.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about European armies' use of spears.
swap.text: At the Battle of Bannockburn, the Scottish under Thomas Randolph effectively used a circular variant of this formation.
swap.clue: At Falkirk, Wallace made use of this military formation, which consisted of tightly packed spearmen arranged in a circle. The name of this military formation can be translated to modern English as "shield wall."
